clue.text: Gave hunter a X?

parts.note: an autograph hunter wants a signature, and an X is the mark someone who cannot write signs with, so giving one is signing for the fan

explanation.surface: Someone appears to have handed a huntsman a kiss, or a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The hunter is an autograph hunter, not someone out with hounds, and X stands in for the signature they collect.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing your name for a fan is exactly what the past-tense verb describes, and an X is a signature by example.

clue.text: Report unopened, given name of director

indicators.note: a thing left unopened has lost its front, so the opening letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a report is the loud noise of a gun, a bang

explanation.surface: A film director's first name is supplied with a report that was never opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes B from BANG, the report of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ang Lee, the Taiwanese film-maker behind Brokeback Mountain, has this as his first name.

clue.text: Theme skittishly put together, free of restrictions

indicators.note: letters put together afresh are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A frivolous theme has been assembled, unconstrained by any rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put together' rearranges all fifteen letters of THEME SKITTISHLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says there is no upper bound on what can be achieved, so one is unconstrained.

clue.text: "I'll take a shot, straight" — sozzled regular, clutching note

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so the anagram wraps round the other piece
sozzled means drunk, so the letters of the word regular stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
NB, nota bene, is a written note to take notice

explanation.surface: A tipsy pub regular, holding a banknote, offers to have a go at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sozzled' gives GUARREL, which 'clutching' wraps round the note. The definition imagines the tube itself speaking: it takes each shot and is straight.
explanation.definitionFit: The tube of a firearm is straight and is what each shot passes along, so it fairly 'takes a shot'.

clue.text: Thawing freezer without first of fingerstalls on cuts from the beginning

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: ab ovo is Latin for 'from the egg', meaning from the very start

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letters are taken away from the word freezer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: on in the sense 'concerning' is RE

explanation.surface: A freezer is defrosting, with fingerstalls involved somehow, cutting things from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' leaves EZER, which 'cuts' the Latin phrase ab ovo ('from the egg'). 'Thawing freezer' looks like one phrase; only the first word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Once the temperature rises past freezing point, ice melts, so being warmer than nought degrees is thawing.

clue.text: Broke out of Reading? Called to account

indicators.note: out of says the next piece is taken away from the first

parts.note: broke means penniless, short of money
reading is one of the three Rs of basic schooling, so it gives R

explanation.surface: Someone escaped from Reading jail and was summoned to answer for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the town and its prison; it is one of 'the three Rs' (reading, writing, arithmetic), so R comes out of HARD UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To be brought before a court or a superior to answer for wrongdoing is this informal phrase.

clue.text: Gloomy GP needs attention

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, DR
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A gloomy family doctor is in need of someone to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old, literary synonym for dismal or dreary.

clue.text: Char kept earning packets

indicators.note: packets means contains, as a packet holds what is inside it

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady kept the pay packets she earned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like a cleaner; it is British slang for a cuppa. 'packets' holds the letters spanning kepT EArning.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is old British slang, from Chinese cha, for the hot drink brewed from leaves.

clue.text: Be ruthless in response to turning nasty with ark

indicators.note: something turning nasty changes its nature, so these letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone acts mercilessly in reaction to an ark that has turned unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning nasty' rearranges IN RESPONSE TO plus ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from warfare: an army sparing no enemy is merciless, and figuratively it means showing no mercy.

clue.text: Moira's strangely heated when he leaves a draught?

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the name are scrambled

parts.note: the name Moira, its possessive ending set aside

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the following word comes out of the synonym

parts.note: a heated argument is a vehement one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Moira becomes oddly hot once a man walks out, perhaps causing a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns MOIRA into AIRMO; 'leaves' takes HE out of VEHEMENT to give VEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a current of moving air felt indoors.

clue.text: Forest spirit resident in tree?

parts.note: a greenwood is a forest in leaf, as in Robin Hood's
pecker is British slang for courage, as in 'keep your pecker up'

explanation.surface: A woodland sprite lives inside a tree, like a dryad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forest spirit' looks like a single definition of a nymph; it is two pieces of wordplay. Pecker is 'spirit' in the British phrase 'keep your pecker up' (stay cheerful).
explanation.definitionFit: This bird nests in holes it drills in trunks, so it lives in a tree; the query marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Aunt in Barcelona's imported two kilos of spiced curry

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tia is the Spanish word for aunt
K is the abbreviation for kilo, so two of them are KK

explanation.surface: A Spanish aunt brought in two kilos of hot curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imported' signals the container; 'Aunt in Barcelona's' asks for the Spanish word, tia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Indian dish of marinated, spice-coated pieces of meat, as in chicken tikka masala.

clue.text: Top Hat star Ginger's last seen dancing for Nag's Head band

indicators.note: letters seen dancing move about into a new order
last picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers in Top Hat, with a pub band playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nag's Head looks like a pub name; it is a horse's head. 'dancing' rearranges TOP HAT STAR plus R (Ginger's last).
explanation.definitionFit: This is the strap of a bridle passing under a horse's throat, a band on the nag's head.

clue.text: Outside gym, "Arse!" — not bad language

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the anagram sits around the other piece
bad means corrupted, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Someone swears outside the gym, and it is not exactly clean language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not bad language' reads as a verdict on the swearing, but 'not' is fodder; 'bad' makes ESRANTO, split by gym class as 'Outside' directs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the constructed international tongue devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Enlivened dish performing intercourse along pier after cycling

indicators.note: along says one string is laid along inside the other, so the anagram runs within the cycled word
cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: performing means acting out, so these letters are put through a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A racy dish involves goings-on along the pier after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cycling' gives RPIE; 'performing' gives ESURRECTION, which 'along' lays inside after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Victorian dish of leftovers baked in a pie, so the food is brought back to life: enlivened.

clue.text: Outrageously hot, so parts I think tasty

indicators.note: parts means splits, so the anagram goes between the two halves

parts.note: 'to me' means in my opinion, I think

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild behaviour, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is so outrageously hot that it divides opinion, but I find it tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outrageously' turns HOT SO into OTHSO, which 'parts' TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means delicious, pleasant to eat.

clue.text: When one asks repeatedly about search

parts.note: 'about' given twice over: on and re both mean concerning
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: Someone keeps asking about a search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly about' supplies two different words for about, ON and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available this way is supplied whenever a person requests it.

clue.text: Discovering Bach, I'll perform 4/4 oratorio

indicators.note: dis-covering removes the covers, the outer letters

parts.note: to do is to perform
4/4 is the time signature called four time, four beats to the bar

explanation.surface: On discovering Bach, a musician plans to perform an oratorio in common time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovering' strips the outer letters from BACH ILL, leaving ACHIL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Michael Tippett's 1941 oratorio, a choral work responding to persecution in the 1930s.

clue.text: Key warmonger invades quiet area with sea inlet?

indicators.note: invades means forces its way into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
the Alt key is on a computer keyboard
Mars is the Roman god of war

explanation.surface: A leading warmonger invades a peaceful district on a sea inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invades' signals the container. Key is the computer key Alt, not a musical key or an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This is coastal land flooded by tides, often crossed by creeks running from the sea; the query flags a loose description.

clue.text: Wet weather affecting visibility? Nothing may be seen through it

indicators.note: something seen through a screen sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mist is weather that limits how far you can see
O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Damp weather cuts visibility so much that nothing can be seen through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen through' puts O inside MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp, slightly wet, is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Supper of cider/tea, with without Lee?

definitions.text: Supper of cider/tea, with without Lee?

parts.words: Supper of cider/tea, with without Lee?
parts.note: Laurie Lee's memoir is Cider with ..., so she sups cider with him; and ... Lee is rhyming slang for tea, so tea without Lee leaves her name

explanation.surface: A puzzling menu note about drinking cider or tea, with or without someone called Lee.
explanation.walkthrough: Two British references: the book 'Cider with Rosie' by Laurie Lee, and cockney rhyming slang 'Rosie Lee', meaning tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl in the memoir's title shares cider with the author, and the slang phrase for a cuppa drops its second word.

clue.text: One ring left enclosing another

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to quit is to leave, so quit means left
another ring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: One ring is left surrounding a second ring, like linked hoops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosing' puts O, a ring shape, inside QUIT; 'another' leans on 'One ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the ring thrown at a peg in the game of the same name.

clue.text: Perhaps the slogan of the Glass Urn Co will be known eventually?

definitions.text: Perhaps the slogan of the Glass Urn Co
definitions.meaning: a maker of see-through urns could boast that the ashes are visible

explanation.surface: An invented funeral firm's motto doubles as a remark that time will tell.
explanation.walkthrough: Remains are the ashes in an urn; in a glass one they can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the outcome is not yet certain but will become clear in due course.

clue.text: A serving of brawn and bread

indicators.note: a serving is a portion, so a portion of the letters is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plate of brawn, a meat jelly, comes with some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A serving of' takes the letters spanning brawN ANd.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is the flat leavened Indian loaf baked in a tandoor, also spelt with one A.

clue.text: Pool table pocket

definitions.meaning: the pool of money staked, the kitty
to sink a ball into a table's pocket in snooker or billiards

explanation.surface: A pocket on a pool table.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a shared fund of stakes, and the verb is the snooker term for sending a ball into a pocket.

clue.text: In high-pressure situation, comic actor's performing with canned laughter

indicators.note: canned means sealed inside a tin, so the laughter goes inside the other letters

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French comic actor, so his name with the possessive gives TATIS
he-he is laughter
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a comedian performs to a laugh track.
explanation.walkthrough: Canned laughter looks like a TV laugh track, but 'canned' is the container signal, putting the laughter after the first letter of the Frenchman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a moment when pressure is mounting and one must perform.
